source_refs.note: Topic 11.7.1 (Structure of Alkenes) with Figures 11.8 to 11.10, printed pages 256-257.

blocks.text: Ethene, C2H4, is the simplest alkene. Each carbon atom in ethene is sp2 hybridised and forms three equivalent sp2 hybrid orbitals lying in the same plane; the unhybridised p orbital lies perpendicular (90 degrees) to the plane of the hybrid orbitals (Figure 11.8). The sp2 orbitals are formed by mixing the 2s orbital with two 2p orbitals, leaving one unhybridised p orbital. In ethene each carbon uses two sp2 orbitals to form two C-H bonds, and the remaining sp2 orbital on each carbon forms the carbon-carbon sigma bond by linear overlap (Figure 11.9). The unhybridised p orbitals of the two carbons, parallel to each other, overlap laterally to form another carbon-carbon bond, the pi bond.

blocks.alt: A carbon atom with three orange sp2 hybrid orbitals spread 120 degrees apart in a flat plane, drawn in perspective, and one green unhybridised 2p orbital with lobes above and below the plane at 90 degrees to it. A box says 2s, 2px and 2py mix to give the three sp2 orbitals and 2pz is left over.

blocks.alt: Ethene on a faint flat plane: two carbons joined by a purple sigma bond along the C-C axis, each with two hydrogens joined by orange sigma bonds at about 120 degrees. Green 2p orbital lobes stand up and down from each carbon, and two green clouds above and below the plane join them: the pi bond.

blocks.long_description: Each carbon in ethene is sp2. Its three sp2 orbitals lie in one plane at 120 degrees and form sigma bonds by end-on overlap: one C-C and two C-H. The unhybridised 2p orbitals stand at right angles to that plane and overlap sideways, above and below it, to form the pi bond. The pi bond holds the molecule flat and stops rotation about C=C.

blocks.text: The two carbon atoms of the double bond and the four atoms attached directly to them lie in the same plane. The sp2 hybridisation gives a trigonal planar arrangement around each carbon with bond angles of approximately 120 degrees, so ethene is a planar molecule (Figure 11.10).

blocks.prompt: Explain the shape of the ethene molecule in terms of its sigma and pi C-C bonds.
blocks.explanation: Each carbon mixes its 2s with two 2p orbitals to give three sp2 orbitals at 120 degrees in one plane, used for two C-H bonds and the C-C sigma bond; the leftover p orbitals stand at right angles to that plane and overlap sideways to form the pi bond. Because the pi bond needs the p orbitals parallel, all six atoms are locked in one plane: a flat, trigonal planar molecule.

items: Ethene: each C sp2 (2s + two 2p), three planar hybrids at 120 degrees, one p orbital at 90 degrees; C=C = sigma (sp2-sp2 linear overlap) + pi (lateral p-p overlap); planar molecule.
